correctness.rationale: This is the census of two-dimensional subspaces of F_5^5 for which all six F_5-projective members are geometrically squarefree, under substitutions of the source coordinates only. The independent program /workspace/branches/6613dc7e-52f9-41ca-95c9-3747ccc72425/independent_census.py generates the unique RREF basis of every plane, uses gcd(f,f') in the affine chart with a separate infinity multiplicity test, and trial-divides by monic irreducibles for the profiles. Thus an affine repeated nonrational root is not missed and a singleton infinity root is included in its factor partition. It partitions the accepted set by images under all 120 normalized invertible source matrices. The full exact run confirms 600 of 781 projective quartics and 3820 of 20306 pencils, orbit-size multiplicities 10:2, 20:1, 40:3, 60:21, 120:20, base-degree frequencies 0:3710, 2:70, 3:40, the full 14-profile frequency table, and split-member histogram 0:3280, 1:540. All 47 computed representatives, orbit sizes, stabilizer orders and base degrees match data/census_catalogue.json lines 15–1003; all profile frequencies match lines 1004–1418. The independent run took 2.215 s (representative 2000-pencil slice 0.281 s); full table and reproduction notes are in independent_census_results.md alongside the program. No uploaded script was executed. Analytically, derivative evaluation on the pencil at a putative rational base point has a rational kernel member, contradicting squarefreeness. Thus two split members would need disjoint four-sets among six source points, so cannot occur. A positive-degree base is a single closed point of degree 2 or 3. The 40 irreducible cubic factors give one pencil apiece. In degree two, the quadratic discriminant conic has ten exterior lines; an irreducible quadratic point lies on no tangent and lies on three secants and three exterior lines, leaving seven allowed lines per each of ten irreducibles. Basepoint-free pencils give a degree-four morphism, separable as inseparable degree would be a power of 5 dividing 4; its six rational target fibers are exactly the reduced members. No comparison is asserted with elliptic-curve isomorphism counts.

evidence: Wall §1 explicitly views basepoint-free pencils as maps P^1(C) to P^1(C) and §2 enumerates strata by ramification symbols, including common-factor cases; the symbols partition multiplicities at geometric branch values, not Frobenius degrees in reduced rational fibers.

Asgarli–Ghioca Theorem 1.3 is an existence result for all-smooth pencils in sufficiently large fields and ambient dimension n>=2. Günay–Lavrauw treat source orbits of cubic pencils over general finite fields in characteristic >3.

evidence: The relevant projective formulation is lines in PG(4,5) avoiding the binary quartic discriminant at all six rational points. The basepoint-free subfamily corresponds to degree-four maps up to source and target projectivities with reduced fibers at rational targets; common-factor cases are excluded from that map formulation.

ArXiv:2312.07118v3 solves the PG(3,q) line problem for twisted-cubic symmetry by associating a single binary quartic to polar dual lines and classifying individual quartic forms. It does not thereby classify lines in the five-dimensional vector space of quartics.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: A target-basis change just presents the same pencil; classifying a member or a pencil of cubics is not equivalent to classifying subspaces of quartic forms with a universal condition on their rational members. Quotienting by all of GL_5 would not preserve the intended orbit invariant.

value.rationale: Degree four over F_5 is the first prime-field characteristic strictly greater than the degree, so it is a small tame test case for reduced fibers at every rational target and for universal smoothness of a pencil of genus-one branch divisors. The full source-orbit catalogue with stabilizers and joint Frobenius profiles supplies a usable classification of that natural arithmetic locus, distinguishes base-divisor cases from degree-four covers, and makes the possible rational-fiber patterns explicit. The full scope, rather than a raw count of convenient sample forms or an arbitrary field slice, justifies the finite computation.
